name: ns-bwa-advisory-lift-duration
stage: simple references on identical eval rows (post-acceptance)

majority_class.definition: majority label fitted on train, measured against this split's labels

global_rate.definition: constant train positive rate; no ranking information, AUC degenerate by construction

persistence_site_prior.definition: the site's as-of lift30 rate over earlier same-site advisories resolved strictly before the instant (the shipped site_prior_lift30_rate feature); global train rate fallback

calendar_county_month.definition: train-estimated (county, issue month) rate with >=5 train rows, county rate then global train rate backoff (identity + seasonal control)

reason_prior.definition: train-estimated positive rate per normalised reason, global rate fallback
train_reasons: public health risk i.e. giardia, crypto

facility_prior.definition: train-estimated positive rate per facility type, global rate fallback

persistence_vs_calendar.note: paired bootstrap on identical rows; an interval containing zero is inconclusive, not parity

calendar_vs_reason.note: paired bootstrap on identical rows; an interval containing zero is inconclusive, not parity

persistence_vs_reason.note: paired bootstrap on identical rows; an interval containing zero is inconclusive, not parity

notes: persistence is the site's own as-of outcome history (the shipped site_prior_lift30_rate); it may embed strictly-earlier eval-era outcomes, which is exactly its information set at the instant - unlike the train-only references
calendar_county_month, reason_prior and facility_prior are estimated only from training-era rows
constant global_rate scores carry no ranking information; its AUC is reported null, not zero
the full model (harness runner baseline) is quoted beside these references when its job exists; it is not computed here
the holdout is sealed: no reference or model in this file reads private/holdout.csv
per-issue-year figures are mandatory reading beside the pooled ones: duration has a measured regime shift around 2020
